nodes.name: VM Consumer
nodes.description: Application or platform-engineer user who declares VirtualMachine custom resources via kubectl / GitOps. Never interacts with the underlying hypervisor SDKs directly — that is the whole point of banlieue.

nodes.name: Platform Operator
nodes.description: Cluster administrator who installs the banlieue CRDs, deploys the controller and provider controllers, and configures Provider CRs with backend credentials.

nodes.name: Management Kubernetes Cluster
nodes.description: Kubernetes cluster (>=1.27) that hosts the banlieue controller and every provider controller. Acts as the control plane for VM lifecycle management across heterogeneous hypervisor backends.

nodes.name: Kubernetes API Server
nodes.description: Management cluster API server. The ONLY communication bus between the banlieue controller and every provider controller. Persists VirtualMachine, VMClass, VMImage, Provider, and infrastructure CRs; mediates every state transition.

nodes.name: banlieue-controller
nodes.description: Main Rust kube-rs controller. Watches VirtualMachine CRs, resolves class/image/providerRef references, creates a backend-specific infrastructure CR carrying the resolved spec, and mirrors status from that infra CR back onto the VirtualMachine. Owns no backend credentials — all backend access is delegated to provider controllers via CRDs.

crd-only-contract.description: Controller MUST NOT speak RPC, REST, gRPC, or any out-of-band protocol to provider controllers. All inter-controller communication is via Kubernetes CRDs and the API server. This is a project non-negotiable (see CLAUDE.md "Non-Negotiables" #1).

least-privilege.description: Controller ServiceAccount holds a ClusterRole scoped to banlieue.io/* and infrastructure.banlieue.io/* CRDs plus events. No cluster-admin, and no Secrets access (security review 2026-07-31 SEC-008: the controller never reads Secrets — providers read their own credentials).

nodes.name: banlieue-operator
nodes.description: Provider lifecycle controller. Watches Provider (one backend instance) and ProviderClass (install metadata: image, resources, workload namespace) CRs, and server-side-applies one Deployment, ServiceAccount, Role, RoleBinding and ClusterRoleBinding per Provider — the per-instance topology of ADR-0003. Each spawned provider pod runs a server-side filtered watch (labelSelector banlieue.io/provider=<name>) so one hung backend cannot stall another. NAMESPACED objects carry an ownerReference to their Provider and are garbage-collected with it; the ClusterRoleBinding cannot (a cluster-scoped dependent with a namespaced owner is deleted immediately by the collector), so a finalizer removes it. Cluster-scoped names are namespace-qualified, because two Providers sharing a name and class in different namespaces would otherwise collide on one binding and fight over its subject. Also prunes superseded workloads by label whenever a Provider's class changes — ADR-0007 ships the immutability policy as OPTIONAL hardening and requires the controller to fall back to delete-and-recreate rather than depend on it. Publishes ProviderClass.status (Providers referencing the class, and a Ready condition reporting whether the shared per-backend ClusterRole exists). Writes only Provider.status.workload — never status.conditions, which the provider's own field manager owns. Holds no backend credentials and never reads Secret contents. See ADR-0012.

crd-only-contract.description: banlieue-operator MUST NOT call provider controllers, the main controller, or any backend SDK. It creates workloads through the Kubernetes API and reads desired state from CRs; the spawned provider then talks to its backend on its own. Same non-negotiable as every other role (CLAUDE.md "Non-Negotiables" #1).

least-privilege.description: The operator ServiceAccount is separate from the main controller's, so the privilege to create Deployments, ServiceAccounts, Roles and RoleBindings never enters the scheduler's identity. Because Kubernetes forbids granting permissions the grantor lacks, the operator ClusterRole holds the union of the permissions it hands to provider Roles rather than the escalate/bind verbs — bounding and making auditable exactly what it can delegate. It can READ ClusterRoles (to report whether a ProviderClass is usable) but never create or modify one; minting the permissions it hands out is the escalation path this design refuses. Per-instance Roles are resourceNames-scoped to the single credentials Secret named by that Provider. No provider identity holds cluster-wide Secret access at all (security review 2026-07-31, CHAIN-002): the shared per-backend ClusterRole is bound cluster-wide to every provider pod, so any Secret rule there would reach every Secret in the cluster and silently defeat the resourceNames narrowing — Secret access therefore lives only in namespaced Roles, `get` only, since resourceNames cannot constrain list/watch.

nodes.name: banlieue-provider-vsphere (planned, Phase 1B)
nodes.description: Provider controller that watches VSphereMachine / VSphereMachineTemplate infrastructure CRs and drives vCenter via the govmomi-equivalent Rust client. Satisfies the CAPI v1beta2 InfraMachine contract so the same provider can also serve CAPI Clusters. Status: PLANNED — Phase 1B in the roadmap; no code in-tree as of this revision.

nodes.name: banlieue-provider-proxmox (planned, Phase 1C)
nodes.description: Provider controller for Proxmox VE clusters. Watches ProxmoxMachine infrastructure CRs and drives the Proxmox HTTP API. Status: PLANNED — Phase 1C.

nodes.name: banlieue-provider-libvirt
nodes.description: Provider controller for libvirt/KVM hosts, speaking libvirt's own RPC protocol through the first-party `banlieue-libvirt` crate (XDR codec + message framing) rather than any third-party client — zero new dependencies, no C library, no FFI. Split by plane (ADR-0011): the CONTROL plane runs in-process — the Provider reconciler connects, lists storage pools and networks, verifies the admin-declared spec.capabilities actually exist, and publishes status.failureDomains[] (one per host, with pools as the interesting sub-structure since libvirt has no datacenter/cluster hierarchy). The DATA plane runs as a Kubernetes Job so bulk disk bytes never flow through the controller process; that Job runs the `banlieue` binary itself, so there is no third-party tools image to pin, trust, or patch. VM lifecycle (a LibvirtMachine InfraMachine CRD) is deliberately out of scope for this increment.

nodes.name: banlieue-imagebuilder
nodes.description: Provider-agnostic controller that turns a VMImage's OCI/Kairos-referenced source (spec.sources[].kind == Url) into a build artifact. Server-side-applies an OSArtifact CR (kairos-operator) requesting either a cloud image (spec.artifacts.cloudImage, for libvirt) or a bootable ISO (spec.artifacts.iso + cloudConfigRef, for vSphere), watches its status.phase, and mirrors readiness into VMImage.status.buildArtifact — a typed top-level field (kind: cloudImage | iso, aligned with kairos OSArtifactKind) distinct from status.perProvider[], so this controller and each provider controller's field manager never contend over the same VMImage.status fields. When VMImage.spec.cloudConfig is set it passes a cloud-config Secret as the OSArtifact cloudConfigRef, baking a default cloud-config into the artifact. Has no knowledge of vSphere, Proxmox, or libvirt; backend-specific conversion (e.g. raw -> VMDK) and per-zone import are each provider's own concern. See ADR-0010 and ADR-0020.

crd-only-contract.description: banlieue-imagebuilder MUST NOT call banlieue-provider-vsphere (or any other provider) directly. The only channel is VMImage.status.buildArtifact (+ the artifacts PVC it references), read by whichever provider controller needs it. Same non-negotiable as every other role (CLAUDE.md "Non-Negotiables" #1).

imagebuild-privilege-domain.description: Image builds run in a dedicated namespace (banlieue-imagebuild) whose Pod Security Standards enforcement is set to `privileged`, because kairos-operator's OSArtifact build pods require privileged:true for loop devices and mounts — which the `baseline` profile denies as well as `restricted`, so no intermediate level exists. Confining that exception keeps enforce:restricted on banlieue-system, where the controller, the operator (an RBAC grantor) and every per-backend provider pod hold cluster-wide or backend credentials. audit/warn remain `restricted` so a NEW privileged workload in the build namespace is still visible. This bounds admission surface, NOT escape capability: a privileged pod can escape to its node regardless of namespace, so node-level isolation (dedicated tainted nodes) remains the outstanding complementary control. See ADR-0016.

nodes.name: kairos-operator (external, not shipped by banlieue)
nodes.description: Upstream Kairos controller (kairos-io/kairos-operator). Watches OSArtifact CRs (build.kairos.io/v1alpha2), pulls/builds the referenced OCI image, and produces a raw disk (status.phase: Pending -> Building -> Exporting -> Ready) written to a PVC it creates. banlieue does not fork or vendor this controller — the platform operator installs it independently (kubectl apply -k, per its own docs) alongside banlieue.

nodes.name: banlieue (single binary)
nodes.description: One Rust executable that packages every controller role. Dispatches subcommands: `banlieue controller` runs the main controller, `banlieue provider <name>` (e.g. `banlieue provider vsphere`) runs a backend provider. Each role lives in an independent library crate with its own dependency graph; providers are gated behind per-provider Cargo features (default = all). One container image ships this binary; Deployments select the role via container args. See ADR-0004.

nodes.name: vSphere / vCenter Backend
nodes.description: Real VMware vSphere environment (vCenter + ESXi hosts) reached by the vSphere provider over HTTPS. The address, credentials, and datacenter are declared in a Provider CR.

nodes.name: Proxmox VE Backend
nodes.description: Real Proxmox VE cluster reached by the Proxmox provider over its HTTPS API on port 8006.

nodes.name: libvirt / KVM Host
nodes.description: libvirt/KVM host reached over libvirt's native RPC protocol on TLS port 16514 (`qemu+tls://host/system`) with mutual TLS. Plaintext TCP 16509 is explicitly NOT supported by this provider even where a host has it enabled: using it would mean implementing SASL DIGEST-MD5 solely to speak an obsolete unencrypted transport — more code for a worse security posture (ADR-0011). The server certificate must carry SANs for every address the host answers on, including the libvirt bridge address (virbr0) that in-cluster workloads dial, because libvirt validates the certificate against the address the client actually dialled.

nodes.name: HashiCorp Vault (KV secrets)
nodes.description: Operator-run HashiCorp Vault, reached by the k0s bootstrap script's `vault` CLI helper (token auth only, read from ambient VAULT_ADDR/VAULT_TOKEN) to fetch the Flux registry credential used to build the flux-operator image-pull secret. Mount and secret path are operator-supplied (VAULT_KV_MOUNT/VAULT_SECRET_PATH), never hardcoded (ADR-0018).

nodes.name: VirtualMachine Custom Resource
nodes.description: Namespaced CRD (banlieue.io/v1alpha1) declaring a backend-agnostic VM: class (→ VMClass), image (→ VMImage), providerRef (→ Provider), and optional userData. The ONLY user-facing API.

nodes.name: Provider Custom Resource
nodes.description: Namespaced CRD (banlieue.io/v1alpha1) declaring the existence of a backend in this cluster: type (vsphere|proxmox|libvirt), endpoint, datacenter, credentialsRef to a Secret. Owned by the platform operator, referenced by VirtualMachine.

nodes.name: ProviderClass Custom Resource
nodes.description: Cluster-scoped CRD (banlieue.io/v1alpha1) carrying install metadata for a backend class: which `banlieue provider <backend>` subcommand to run, the container image, workload namespace, replicas, resources, node placement, logging, and any additional RBAC rules. Referenced by Provider.spec.providerClassRef. Cluster-scoped because it is a platform-owner decision about what banlieue runs, consumed by Provider CRs in any tenant namespace. See ADR-0012.

nodes.name: VMClass Custom Resource
nodes.description: Cluster-scoped CRD (banlieue.io/v1alpha1) declaring a flavour: CPU count, memory, disk shape. Referenced by VirtualMachine.spec.class by name.

nodes.name: VMImage Custom Resource
nodes.description: Cluster-scoped CRD (banlieue.io/v1alpha1) declaring a boot image and its source. Referenced by VirtualMachine.spec.image by name; resolved by the provider against its backend's native image catalog. spec.sources[].kind == Url sources are built by banlieue-imagebuilder; status.buildArtifact (typed cloudImage | iso, set by banlieue-imagebuilder) and status.perProvider[] (set by each provider, incl. per-zone import progress in .zones[]) are separate fields owned by separate field managers. spec.cloudConfig supplies a default cloud-config baked into the built artifact. See ADR-0010 and ADR-0020.

nodes.name: OSArtifact Custom Resource (external, kairos-operator)
nodes.description: Namespaced CRD (build.kairos.io/v1alpha2) owned by kairos-operator, not banlieue. banlieue-imagebuilder server-side-applies one per Url-sourced VMImage (field manager banlieue.io/imagebuilder) requesting spec.artifacts.cloudImage=true (libvirt) or spec.artifacts.iso=true with a cloudConfigRef (vSphere; kairos runs `auroraboot build-iso --cloud-config`), and reads its status.phase / resulting artifacts PVC. banlieue never modifies kairos-operator's own reconciliation of this object.

nodes.name: Infrastructure Machine CR (VSphereMachine, etc.)
nodes.description: Namespaced CRD (infrastructure.banlieue.io/v1alpha1) created by the banlieue-controller as the message to the provider. Satisfies the CAPI v1beta2 InfraMachine contract so the same provider can serve both banlieue and CAPI. Status is owned by the provider; the banlieue controller mirrors it back onto the VirtualMachine.

nodes.name: Infrastructure Cluster CR (VSphereCluster)
nodes.description: Namespaced CRD (infrastructure.banlieue.io/v1alpha1) satisfying the CAPI v1beta2 InfraCluster contract. A CAPI Cluster.spec.infrastructureRef points at it. The banlieue-controller reconciles it by aggregating status.failureDomains[] from one or more Provider CRs into the CAPI v1beta2 failure-domain list — so one Kubernetes cluster can span multiple vCenters. No backend access: pure CRD aggregation of Provider status. See ADR-0002.

nodes.name: CAPI Cluster / MachineDeployment (external)
nodes.description: Upstream Cluster API objects (cluster.x-k8s.io): Cluster, MachineDeployment, and a control-plane object. NOT owned by banlieue — owned by CAPI core and a control-plane provider (k0smotron for k0s). 'replicas: N' on these objects, spread across the InfraCluster's failure domains, is how banlieue provisions a Kubernetes cluster (ADR-0001). banlieue is CAPI's infrastructure provider, not its cluster controller.

nodes.name: Cluster API core + control-plane provider (k0smotron)
nodes.description: Upstream CAPI controllers (cluster, machineset, machinedeployment) plus a control-plane/bootstrap provider — k0smotron for k0s. Reads VSphereCluster.status.failureDomains, balances Machines across them (count-based round-robin), and mints VSphereMachines from a VSphereMachineTemplate. banlieue does NOT ship these; the platform operator installs them. This is what lets any CAPI consumer (kubeadm, RKE2, k0smotron) use banlieue as an infra provider.

nodes.name: k0s Bootstrap Script
nodes.description: scripts/bootstrap-k0s-cluster.sh — stands up the MANAGEMENT k0s cluster that runs the banlieue controllers and kairos-operator (the substrate `banlieue bootstrap` later installs onto; not a workload provisioned through banlieue). Pluggable BACKEND: `libvirt` clones/installs Kairos VMs via virt-install on a KVM host; `vsphere` clones cluster-specific Kairos templates via govc against a vCenter, spreading nodes evenly across compute clusters so each is an etcd failure domain. Installs k0s with k0sctl. No environment-specific identifier is committed — every value comes from the GOVC_* environment, govc discovery, or an untracked operator config (ADR-0017). An opt-in `flux` step (FLUX_ENABLED=true), backend-agnostic, fetches a registry credential from Vault and pushes flux-operator + flux-core manifests onto the first controller node (ADR-0018).

relationships.description: The single `banlieue` binary is composed of every controller role. Each role is invoked as a subcommand (`banlieue controller`, `banlieue operator`, `banlieue provider vsphere`, …) and lives in an independent library crate; the binary only dispatches. The same binary also installs the platform via `banlieue bootstrap` (ADR-0013), building CRDs from its own Rust types so the schemas applied always match the binary applying them. See ADR-0004.
The management cluster hosts the banlieue controller, banlieue-operator, every provider controller, banlieue-imagebuilder, kairos-operator, and the Kubernetes API server itself.

Every banlieue CR (VirtualMachine, Provider, ProviderClass, VMClass, VMImage, infrastructure machines) plus the external OSArtifact CR is persisted by the management-cluster API server in etcd. The API server is therefore the bus AND the source of truth for state.
VM consumer authors and applies VirtualMachine CRs (and references VMClass / VMImage / Provider by name).

Platform operator authors ProviderClass CRs (what banlieue runs for a backend class), Provider CRs (one backend instance), and the backing credentials Secret. Applying a Provider is what causes banlieue-operator to spawn that backend's controller — no manifest editing required. Consumers never see provider credentials.

Platform operator authors the CAPI Cluster, control-plane object, MachineDeployment(s), the VSphereCluster (InfraCluster), and a VSphereMachineTemplate to provision a Kubernetes (k0s) cluster. 'replicas: N' on the CAPI objects drives failure-domain spread.
VM consumer applies manifests via kubectl / GitOps to the management-cluster Kubernetes API.
Platform operator applies CRDs, Provider CRs, and the controller deployment via kubectl / GitOps.

banlieue-controller watches VirtualMachine / Provider / VMClass / VMImage / VSphereCluster CRs, server-side-applies infrastructure machine CRs, watches their status, and patches VirtualMachine status with the mirrored conditions. It also reconciles VSphereCluster (InfraCluster) by aggregating selected Providers' status.failureDomains[] into the CAPI v1beta2 failure-domain list — reading Provider status only, no backend access.

banlieue-operator watches ProviderClass and Provider CRs and server-side-applies the per-instance provider workload (Deployment, ServiceAccount, Role, RoleBinding) with field manager banlieue.io/operator, then mirrors readiness into Provider.status.workload. It never contacts the spawned provider, the main controller, or any backend — only the K8s API.
vSphere provider controller watches VSphereMachine infrastructure CRs and patches their .status. NEVER speaks to the banlieue controller directly — the K8s API is the bus.
Proxmox provider controller watches ProxmoxMachine infrastructure CRs and patches their .status. Same CRD-only contract as the vSphere provider.
libvirt provider controller watches LibvirtMachine infrastructure CRs and patches their .status. Same CRD-only contract.

CAPI core + control-plane provider (k0smotron) watch Cluster / MachineDeployment / VSphereCluster, read VSphereCluster.status.failureDomains, and create Machine + VSphereMachine objects spread across those failure domains. Pure Kubernetes API — banlieue never talks to CAPI out of band.

banlieue-imagebuilder watches VMImage for spec.sources[].kind==Url entries, server-side-applies the matching OSArtifact CR (field manager banlieue.io/imagebuilder; cloudImage or iso artifact + cloudConfigRef resolved from VMImage.spec.cloudConfig), watches that OSArtifact's status, and patches VMImage.status.buildArtifact. Never calls kairos-operator or any provider controller directly — only the K8s API.
kairos-operator watches OSArtifact CRs, builds the requested raw disk, and patches OSArtifact.status.phase. Owned and reconciled entirely by kairos-operator; banlieue only ever reads this status.

vSphere provider talks to vCenter over HTTPS to create, query, update, and destroy VMs.  Iteration 2 also introspects each cluster's reachable datastores (incl. SDRS datastore-cluster membership) and networks (standard + distributed port groups) to populate Provider.status.failureDomains[].attributes.availableStorageClasses / availableNetworkClasses (ADR-0019). Both planes use this one transport: the in-process Provider reconciler for cheap list/introspection calls, and a per-failure-domain image-import Job (for VMImage.status.buildArtifact.kind==iso) that mounts the shared artifacts PVC, uploads the ISO to that zone's datastore, then creates an empty EFI VM, attaches the ISO, and MarkAsTemplate — Content Library optional, default off (ADR-0020).

tls-trust-byoc.description: The vSphere provider owns the HTTP transport (Bring-Your-Own-Client): it builds the reqwest::Client and injects it via vim_rs ClientBuilder::http_client, rather than letting vim_rs construct one. banlieue therefore controls TLS trust establishment end to end — honouring Provider.spec.connection.caBundle (a value-or-source: inline PEM, or a configMapRef / secretRef key defaulting to ca.crt; exactly one, enforced controller-side and by a ValidatingAdmissionPolicy per ADR-0007), added as root certificate(s); insecureSkipTLSVerify is a separate, explicit opt-out (gated behind the banlieue.io/allow-insecure-tls annotation by an admission policy, security review 2026-07-31). Credentials and caBundle sources are read by name in the Provider's namespace through the operator-built per-instance Role (resourceNames-scoped, ADR-0003); the shared provider ClusterRole grants no Secret/ConfigMap access at all (security review 2026-07-31 CHAIN-002). The transport is OpenSSL-free: vim_rs 0.5 (reqwest 0.13/rustls) is consumed in BYOC mode and the reqwest client uses the rustls ring provider shared with kube, installed once as the process default (ADR-0009). See ADR-0008 (BYOC runtime design) and ADR-0009 (0.5 migration + build end state).

relationships.description: Proxmox provider talks to Proxmox VE over its HTTPS API on port 8006.

libvirt provider talks to libvirtd over libvirt's native RPC protocol on TLS port 16514. Both planes use this one transport: the in-process Provider reconciler for cheap list calls, and the import Job for streaming volume data.

libvirt-mutual-tls.description: Mutual TLS is the only supported libvirt transport: the client certificate is the authentication mechanism — no password, no SASL, no DIGEST-MD5. The crypto posture is inherited unchanged from the vSphere BYOC work (rustls with the ring provider, no OpenSSL), so libvirt support adds no new TLS stack. Client credentials are provisioned by scripts/bootstrap-libvirt-tls.sh and delivered as a Kubernetes Secret.

relationships.description: The vSphere backend of the bootstrap script clones the management cluster's node VMs from cluster-specific Kairos templates and reconfigures them (static networking via guestinfo, cloud-init via guestinfo.userdata, CPU/memory/disk) over the vCenter API, using ambient GOVC_* credentials. vCenter host, datacenter, resource pools, datastores, and port groups are discovered at runtime, never committed (ADR-0017).

The libvirt backend of the bootstrap script creates the management cluster's node VMs on a KVM host via virt-install and an unattended Kairos install-from-ISO, then installs k0s with k0sctl (ADR-0017).

The bootstrap script's opt-in flux step fetches a registry credential from HashiCorp Vault via the `vault` CLI (token auth, KV mount/path operator-supplied) to build the flux-operator image-pull secret (ADR-0018).

flows.name: Create a VirtualMachine
flows.description: User applies a VirtualMachine CR; the banlieue controller resolves its references and creates a backend-specific infrastructure CR; the matching provider controller observes the infra CR, provisions on its backend, and patches status; the banlieue controller mirrors the status back onto the VirtualMachine.

transitions.description: VM consumer kubectl-applies a VirtualMachine CR with class, image, and providerRef. Persisted in etcd via the management-cluster API server.
banlieue-controller watch fires. Controller resolves the named VMClass, VMImage, and Provider; computes the desired infrastructure spec.

banlieue-controller server-side-applies a VSphereMachine (or ProxmoxMachine / LibvirtMachine) CR with the resolved spec, ownerReference back to the VirtualMachine, and the controller's field manager 'banlieue.io/controller'.
The matching provider controller's watch fires on the new infrastructure CR. Provider reads its spec.
Provider talks to its backend (vCenter / Proxmox / libvirt) to create the underlying VM, attach disks, attach network, power on.
Provider patches infrastructure-CR .status with CAPI v1beta2 conditions (Ready, addresses[], providerID, etc.) using its own field manager (e.g. 'banlieue.io/provider-vsphere').
banlieue-controller watch on infrastructure CRs fires. Controller mirrors the status (Ready, conditions, addresses) onto VirtualMachine.status — never sets Ready=true on its own.

no-rpc-between-controllers.description: Every transition in this flow is a Kubernetes API call. There is no direct controller-to-controller communication. Enforces the CRD-only contract.

flows.name: Swap a VirtualMachine's backend (least-touch)
flows.description: User changes a single field — VirtualMachine.spec.providerRef.name — to repoint a VM from one backend to another. The banlieue controller tears down the old infrastructure CR and creates a new one of the right kind on the new provider. The user's manifest does not otherwise change. This is the canonical demonstration of banlieue's abstraction principle.

transitions.description: VM consumer patches VirtualMachine.spec.providerRef.name (e.g. 'prod-vsphere' → 'prod-proxmox').
banlieue-controller observes the spec change. Detects that the existing infrastructure CR no longer matches the desired provider type.
Controller deletes the stale VSphereMachine CR; the vSphere provider observes the deletion and tears down the backend VM via finalizer; ownerReference cascade clears the infra CR.
Controller server-side-applies a ProxmoxMachine CR with the same uniform spec. The Proxmox provider observes the new CR and provisions on Proxmox VE.
Provider patches new infra-CR status; controller mirrors Ready=true back onto the VirtualMachine. Consumer's manifest still looks identical except for one field.

least-touch.description: Demonstrates banlieue's user-facing invariant: changing the backend MUST NOT require changes outside spec.providerRef.name. Any feature that breaks this is rejected.

flows.name: Delete a VirtualMachine (finalizer cleanup)
flows.description: Deletion is gated by two finalizers (controller, provider) to guarantee that the backend VM is torn down BEFORE the CR is removed from etcd. No leaks.

transitions.description: VM consumer kubectl-deletes the VirtualMachine. API server sets deletionTimestamp; CR persists because the controller finalizer 'banlieue.io/virtualmachine' is still attached.
banlieue-controller observes deletionTimestamp. Issues a delete on the owned infrastructure machine CR.
Provider observes deletionTimestamp on its infra CR (its own finalizer is attached). Begins backend teardown.
Provider talks to the backend (vCenter / Proxmox / libvirt) to power-off, detach storage, and delete the underlying VM. Confirms via backend API.
Provider clears its finalizer; infra CR is garbage-collected by the API server.
banlieue-controller observes the infra CR disappear; clears its own finalizer on the VirtualMachine; CR is garbage-collected. No backend leak.

finalizer-ordering.description: Two-level finalizer chain (controller-side waits for provider-side to clear) guarantees the backend VM is destroyed before the CR is. A crash anywhere in the chain is replay-safe because reconciliation is idempotent.

flows.name: Provision a Kubernetes cluster via CAPI (banlieue as infra provider)
flows.description: The platform operator provisions a k0s cluster by applying upstream CAPI objects plus banlieue's VSphereCluster (InfraCluster) and a VSphereMachineTemplate. banlieue does NOT own cluster lifecycle — CAPI + a control-plane provider (k0smotron) do. banlieue's job is to advertise failure domains (VSphereCluster) and realise each machine (VSphereMachine). 'replicas: N' spread across failure domains is how a tier (e.g. 6/6 'platinum') is expressed (ADR-0001).

transitions.description: Operator applies a CAPI Cluster (infrastructureRef → VSphereCluster), a control-plane object, MachineDeployment(s) with replica counts, the VSphereCluster, and a VSphereMachineTemplate.

banlieue-controller's VSphereCluster watch fires. It resolves the selected Provider CRs (providerRefs / providerSelector), aggregates their status.failureDomains[] into VSphereCluster.status.failureDomains (CAPI v1beta2 list), applies controlPlaneFailureDomainSelector, and sets initialization.provisioned + Ready. No vCenter access.

CAPI core + control-plane provider read VSphereCluster.status.failureDomains and balance the requested replicas across them (count-based round-robin), creating one Machine + one VSphereMachine per placement from the VSphereMachineTemplate, each stamped with spec.failureDomain.

The vSphere provider's VSphereMachine watch fires for each new machine (the existing Create-a-VirtualMachine machine path). It maps the failure domain to a (datacenter, cluster) and reads the resolved spec.
Provider clones the VM into the chosen compute cluster's resource pool and powers it on. vSphere DRS selects the ESXi host within that cluster — banlieue does not pick the host.

Provider patches VSphereMachine.status (provisioned, providerID, addresses); CAPI mirrors it up to the Machine, and the control-plane provider (k0smotron) joins the nodes into the k0s cluster once the control plane is reachable.

capi-native-failure-domain-spread.description: Cluster-level replica management and failure-domain spread are delegated to CAPI; banlieue only advertises failure domains (InfraCluster) and realises machines (InfraMachine). banlieue ships NO native cluster/tier controller. This keeps banlieue reusable by any CAPI consumer and avoids duplicating MachineSet/control-plane logic (ADR-0001).

flows.name: Build a VMImage from an OCI/Kairos image and import it per zone
flows.description: A VMImage with a spec.sources[].kind==Url entry (an OCI-referenced Kairos image, e.g. from a nightly build pipeline) is turned into a typed build artifact — a raw cloud image for libvirt, a bootable ISO with a baked-in default cloud-config for vSphere — by banlieue-imagebuilder via kairos-operator, then imported into every zone of a matching vSphere Provider by banlieue-provider-vsphere as a marked template. The two controllers never call each other; VMImage.status.buildArtifact is the entire handoff. See ADR-0010 and ADR-0020.

transitions.description: Platform operator (or a nightly CI job authenticated as one) applies/updates a VMImage with a Url source pointing at the newly-built Kairos OCI image, optionally with spec.cloudConfig (secretRef) and spec.template (folder / network / disk / force knobs) for the vSphere template.

banlieue-imagebuilder's VMImage watch fires. It server-side-applies an OSArtifact CR requesting a cloud image (libvirt sources) or an ISO with artifacts.cloudConfigRef resolved from spec.cloudConfig (vsphere sources), and sets VMImage.status.buildArtifact.phase=Building.

kairos-operator's OSArtifact watch fires. It pulls the OCI image and builds the artifact — a raw disk, or auroraboot build-iso with --cloud-config for an ISO — writing it to a PVC it creates, progressing status.phase through Building -> Exporting -> Ready.

banlieue-imagebuilder's OSArtifact watch fires on the Ready transition. It patches VMImage.status.buildArtifact with kind (cloudImage | iso), phase=Ready, the artifacts PVC reference, the artifact file name, and the checksum.

banlieue-provider-vsphere's VMImage watch fires. It finds a Url-kind vsphere source with buildArtifact.phase==Ready and kind==iso and begins a per-zone import for each of its Providers' status.failureDomains[].

For each zone, an image-import Job (banlieue binary's image-import subcommand, imagebuild namespace, artifacts PVC mounted read-only) verifies the ISO against buildArtifact.checksum, uploads it to the zone's datastore — reusing the datastore-cluster member already holding it, else the emptiest — ensures the spec.template.folder, and creates the template: empty EFI VM (pvscsi disk from spec.template.disk, vmxnet3 NIC on the spec.template.network or zone port group), ISO attached as CD-ROM, then MarkAsTemplate.

banlieue-provider-vsphere patches VMImage.status.perProvider[].zones[] with per-zone readiness and resolvedRef (the template's [datastore] folder/name), using its own field manager — never touching status.buildArtifact.

crd-only-build-handoff.description: banlieue-imagebuilder and banlieue-provider-vsphere coordinate purely through VMImage.status: buildArtifact (imagebuilder's field) and perProvider[] (each provider's field) never contend because SSA tracks ownership per field, not per object. The only non-CRD coupling is the same-namespace artifacts PVC the artifact's bytes live in — the control channel (when/whether to act) stays CRD-only; only the artifact's bytes travel outside a CRD field, since a CRD cannot carry a multi-hundred-MB disk image or ISO.

flows.name: Import a built raw disk into libvirt storage pools
flows.description: The libvirt half of ADR-0010's pipeline: once banlieue-imagebuilder has produced a raw disk, banlieue-provider-libvirt imports it into each storage pool the Provider advertises. Demonstrates the same build-then-import split as the vSphere path, on a backend that needs no proprietary SDK. See ADR-0011.

transitions.description: Platform operator applies a Provider of class `libvirt` (endpoint qemu+tls://host/system, caBundle + client-certificate credentialsRef) declaring the storage pools and networks the host exposes.
banlieue-provider-libvirt's Provider watch fires. It reads the CA bundle and client certificate from the referenced ConfigMap/Secret.
Provider connects over mutual TLS and lists storage pools and networks, verifying the admin's declared capabilities actually exist on the host. Two in-process RPC calls — no Job.
Provider patches status.failureDomains[] (one per libvirt host) carrying the verified pools and networks, and sets Ready.

A VMImage with a libvirt Url source reaches status.buildArtifact.phase=Ready with kind==cloudImage (written by banlieue-imagebuilder, never by this provider). The provider's VMImage watch fires and creates one import Job per target pool, running the banlieue binary itself with the artifacts PVC mounted read-only.

The import Job creates a raw storage volume sized to the artifact and streams the disk bytes into it over the same TLS connection, using libvirt's stream protocol. Bulk data flows from the Job, never through the controller.
Provider patches VMImage.status.perProvider[].zones[] with per-pool readiness, using field manager banlieue.io/provider-libvirt — never touching status.buildArtifact.

control-plane-data-plane-split.description: Capability probing (list pools, list networks) runs in-process because it is two cheap RPC calls; bulk disk transfer runs in a Kubernetes Job because a multi-hundred-MB stream must never flow through the controller process, where it would compete with reconcile latency and pin memory. The Job runs the banlieue binary itself rather than a third-party virsh/qemu-img image, so there is no external image to pin, trust, or keep patched, and the same banlieue-libvirt code is exercised in both roles.

flows.name: Register a backend and have its controller provisioned automatically
flows.description: The flow that makes banlieue an operator in the strict sense: a platform owner declares a ProviderClass once (image, resources, namespace), then applies a Provider CR per backend instance. banlieue-operator turns each Provider into a dedicated Deployment + ServiceAccount + Role + RoleBinding, so one hung or slow backend cannot stall reconciliation for any other and each pod holds exactly one backend's credentials. Deleting the Provider garbage-collects the whole set via owner references. See ADR-0003 (per-instance topology) and ADR-0012.

transitions.description: Platform operator installs the platform with `banlieue bootstrap operator` — namespace, CRDs built from the binary's own Rust types, controller and operator RBAC and Deployments, plus one ProviderClass per backend compiled into the binary (ADR-0013). `--dry-run` emits the same YAML for a GitOps repo instead of applying it.
Platform operator applies a Provider CR naming its ProviderClass, the backend endpoint, and a credentials Secret in the same namespace.

banlieue-operator's Provider watch fires. It resolves the referenced ProviderClass and server-side-applies a ServiceAccount, a Role scoped by resourceNames to just that Provider's credentials Secret, a RoleBinding, and a Deployment running `banlieue provider <backend>` — all carrying an ownerReference back to the Provider.

The spawned provider pod starts, acquires its own leader-election Lease (banlieue-provider-<class>-<provider-name>), and begins a server-side filtered watch on labelSelector banlieue.io/provider=<name> so its informer cache holds only its own infra objects.

The provider logs in to its backend with the one credential it can read, introspects the inventory, and publishes reachable failure domains to Provider.status.failureDomains — the input the main controller's scheduler matches VirtualMachines against.

banlieue-operator's Deployment watch fires as replicas become ready and mirrors readiness into Provider.status.workload. It deliberately does not write status.conditions — that list is owned by the provider's own field manager, and a plain list without x-kubernetes-list-type:map cannot be merged per-entry by two managers.

least-privilege.description: Per-instance isolation is the security property this flow exists to deliver: one Deployment, ServiceAccount and Lease per backend, each Role resourceNames-scoped to a single credentials Secret. A compromised provider pod holds exactly one backend's credentials, and per-backend NetworkPolicy becomes expressible because a pod has exactly one egress target.

flows.name: Upgrade every backend of a class with one edit
flows.description: The payoff of putting install metadata on a ProviderClass rather than on each Provider: bumping a fleet is a one-object edit, not one edit per backend. banlieue-operator watches ProviderClass and maps each edit back to every Provider referencing it, so the change lands at once instead of waiting on a periodic requeue. The same path makes un-pausing a class immediate. See ADR-0012.

transitions.description: Platform operator edits one field — `kubectl patch providerclass vsphere -p '{"spec":{"image":{"tag":"v0.2.0"}}}'`. To canary a single backend instead, they create a second class pinning the new image and repoint one Provider at it.

banlieue-operator's ProviderClass watch fires. kube calls the mapper synchronously, so it cannot list Providers itself — it reads the controller's own reflector store, already maintained for the primary Provider watch, and emits one reconcile request per referencing Provider. Without this the edit would only be noticed on the next periodic requeue.

Each Provider reconciles: the workload is re-applied with the new image and the Deployment rolls. If the edit changed the Provider's CLASS rather than the class's contents, the derived name changes too, so the superseded workload is pruned by label — including the ClusterRoleBinding, which no owner reference can reclaim and a name-based cleanup could never find again.

The operator publishes ProviderClass.status: how many Providers reference this class, and a Ready condition reporting whether the shared per-backend ClusterRole exists. That surfaces an unusable class in `kubectl get providerclasses` before any Provider is created, rather than as 403s in a provider pod's log afterwards.

least-touch.description: Upgrading N backends is one edit, not N. The image lives on the class precisely so the fleet-wide operation stays a single object change — the same least-touch invariant that keeps a backend swap confined to spec.providerRef.

code-first-crds.description: All CRDs are generated from the Rust type system in crates/banlieue-api via the crdgen binary; YAML in deploy/crds/ is never hand-edited. Prevents drift between Rust types and the schemas the API server validates against.

capi-v1beta2-infra-machine-contract.description: Every banlieue provider's infrastructure CRD satisfies the upstream Cluster API v1beta2 InfraMachine contract. Buys a battle-tested status model AND lets the same provider also serve CAPI Clusters without modification. CAPI discovers compliance via the CRD-level label cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta2=v1alpha1, emitted onto every infrastructure.banlieue.io CRD by crdgen post-processing (ADR-0005) since kube-derive cannot set CRD labels.

capi-v1beta2-infra-cluster-contract.description: banlieue's InfraCluster CRD (VSphereCluster) satisfies the upstream Cluster API v1beta2 InfraCluster contract: status.initialization.provisioned, optional spec.controlPlaneEndpoint, and status.failureDomains as a v1beta2 list ({name, controlPlane, attributes}). It uniquely aggregates failure domains from multiple Provider CRs, so one cluster can span several vCenters. Reconciled by the main controller with no backend access (ADR-0002). The CRD carries the cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta2=v1alpha1 contract label emitted by crdgen (ADR-0005).

supply-chain-scanning.description: Repository is scanned by CodeQL (SAST on Rust), cargo-deny (RustSec advisories + license allow-list + source restrictions), and OpenSSF Scorecard. SPDX license identifiers on every source file.

release-artifact-provenance.description: Every release ships the `banlieue` binary (multi-arch, signed) plus distroless and Chainguard container images, each with: CycloneDX SBOM (binary via cargo-cyclonedx, image via syft/anchore), Cosign keyless (OIDC) signatures, GitHub build-provenance attestations, SLSA Build L3 provenance (slsa-github-generator) for the binary tarballs, and an OpenVEX document (vexctl-merged from .vex/, Cosign-attested to each image digest and consumed by the Grype scan as `grype --vex`). Grype results upload to GitHub Code Scanning as SARIF. VEX statements are derived automatically by the banlieue-vex crate's auto-vex-presence (SBOM-absence) and auto-vex-reachability (binary symbol-import) tools and merged with curated .vex/*.json. Build logic is Makefile-driven; firestoned/github-actions composites are reused; third-party actions are SHA-pinned (SLSA generator pinned to a release tag).

admission-policy-validation.description: Invariants the code-first CRD schema cannot express — VirtualMachine.classRef/imageRef and Provider.providerClassRef immutability — are enforced at admission via ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (CEL, evaluated in the API server, GA in Kubernetes 1.30+). The same mechanism carries the security chain-breakers of the 2026-07-31 review: Provider connection hardening (https endpoints, no userinfo, opt-in-gated insecureSkipTLSVerify), credentialsRef authorization via the CEL authorizer variable, and digest-pinned, registry-allowlisted VMImage importFrom sources (parameter ConfigMap). No validating webhook: no extra always-on service, no TLS cert rotation, no API-request-path availability dependency — consistent with banlieue's no-RPC / no-extra-services posture. Shipped as optional, separately-applied manifests under deploy/admission/ with Deny bindings (Warn/Audit report-only roll-out path). See ADR-0007.
